page: Amazon Web Services c7i.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8488C processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz and is equipped with a 105 MB L3 cache. The instance includes 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the c7i.2xlarge in the average performance tier for most compute and memory tasks, with some notable strengths. Single-threaded gzip compression performs strongly at 32.73 GB/sec, and Geekbench text processing also registers in the top 25% tier with a score of 2743.0. However, the Passmark memory score of 1800.86 is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% tier, which aligns with the uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths of 47.98 GB/sec and 44.81 GB/sec respectively. For machine learning tasks, the CPU's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) support prompt processing of 51.04 tokens/sec on a 7B LLM model, though text generation on the same model is limited to a weaker 6.32 tokens/sec.

Given its compute-focused hardware profile, the c7i.2xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that demand dedicated CPU resources without requiring massive memory footprints or local NVMe storage. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX makes it highly suitable for compute-intensive tasks, including software compilation, text processing, and light machine learning inference. It is also well-suited for static web serving and Redis database operations, where it achieves 10.98 million SET operations per second.
